reporting: Every 12 hours plus extra readings in some storms until May 2025; hourly plus extra storm readings since Oct 2025
history_and_issues: Outages: Jun 23 - Oct 6, 2020; Nov 24 - Dec 15, 2021; May 29 - Oct 16, 2025. Sensor faults: Jul 15, 2022 (readings to about 16.7 ft); Aug 18, 2022 (one-reading spike to 4.56 ft). When it switches from hourly to faster readings in a storm, the rising-fast check can miss the rise (RISING_FAST_BASIS.md section 8).
tide_check: staff (Oct 16, 2026): tidally influenced at Orange Memorial Park. Checked against the Alameda tide (Oct 17, 2026): this gauge's reading does not follow the tide, in dry weather or in storms. Dry weather (Oct 2025 - Jun 2026, hourly): the reading stayed under 0.3 ft and did not rise with the tide, even at tides of 8.1-8.3 ft NAVD88 (about 2 ft above the average daily high tide). Storms (62 rises above 1 ft, Oct 2021 - Jun 2026): peaks came at high and low tide alike, and the creek drained just as fast at high tide (typically half way back down within an hour). Example: Jan 4, 2026, the creek fell from 2.63 ft to under half that within 10 minutes during an 8.2 ft high tide with 1.2 ft of storm surge. The tide may still back up the creek further downstream, but this gauge does not show it. Not yet checked against rain records; 2021-22 storms had too few readings to test
rise_basis: Tidal since Oct 16, 2026 (staff): the rain condition now applies. Record not usable yet: the gauge sent one reading every 12 hours until 2025 (hourly since), with outages Jun–Oct 2020, Nov 24 – Dec 15, 2021 and May 29 – Oct 16, 2025. 3 of 7 Monitoring crossings warned, but 2 of the 7 are sensor faults (Jul 15 and Aug 18, 2022), and the rule misses the rise when Colma switches from hourly to faster readings.
source: FEWS data archive and history pulls, Oct 15, 2026 (RISING_FAST_BASIS.md); tidal: Summer (OneShoreline), Oct 16, 2026
